Further, clear policies have to be formulated regarding punitive measures and how they may be enforced. If GenAI tools are allowed, the instructor should be clear which tools are allowed and in what capacity.

Instructors should align their course policies with their college’s academic misconduct policies.

GenAI is changing rapidly, and n

ew tools will become available. Course policies therefore need to be provisional and subject to change. Several principles can guide instructors to develop course policies appropriate for their contexts:
Protect cognitive dimension of learning: GenAI should enhance, not hinder, learning.
Responsibility for content: Students are responsible for all content (ideas, facts, citations), however the work is generated. (Note: Chat GPT can generate untrue, biased, inaccurate, and hallucinatory content.)
Require ethical transparency: Students should be transparent about how they use GenAI and adhere to standards of academic integrity.
Explain academic misconduct: Instructors should distinguish betwee

n allowed and disallowed uses of GenAI, including how, when, and why GenAI may (not) be used.
Course policies might fall into one of three categories:
Specific uses of GenAI are encouraged (generating ideas, editing, translating, outlining)
Specific uses of GenAI are allowed if students clearly distinguish between their original work and GenAI output (highlighting output, tracking changes in GenAI output)
Any use of GenAI constitutes academic misconduct.
Align with the university’s principles for honesty, candor, openness, and integrity in scholarship and research, including appropriate disclosure and citation where AI has been used.

What Information We Collect
ITS AI Services collect your input into the AI applications when you directly provide it to us, such as when you log in, enter prompts or questions, and upload documents.
ITS AI Services also capture some information about you automatically when you use the services. Automatically collected information may include:
The Internet domain you use
Your device’s IP address
Your Internet Service Provider
Your Cell Phone Service Provider
The type of cell phone
The type of browser
The date and time of visit
The address of the website that linked to ITS AI Services
Information about your role at the U-M and other related HR and student data via Single Sign On.
Crash reports

and debugging logs
How We Use Personal Information
The University of Michigan uses information about your interactions with ITS AI Services to:
Monitor performance and make improvements to functionality and user experience.
Provide support for questions about using the web applications or troubleshoot issues.
Enforce token quota limitation and enable internal billing.
Provide persistence of user prompt history across sessions with the ITS AI services.
We use de-identified and/or aggregated information to:
Monitor trends on the use of the tool to inform the product roadmap.
Monitor application performance to inform improvements to the application, such as device and browser compatibility, ap

plication features, etc.
Develop projections for future usage and anticipate service costs.
The use of personal information collected by this service is safeguarded through several mechanisms, including Information Assurance and U-M policies, such as Privacy and the Need to Monitor and Access Records (SPG 601.11) and Institutional Data Stewardship Policy (SPG 601.12).
With Whom We Share Personal Information
We do not sell or license your personal information collected here. To operate the ITS AI Services, however, we must share your prompt data with the cloud vendor utilized to host the ITS AI services. 
Specifically, we share your information with Microsoft Azure Services and Google. Learn

basis.evidenceSnippet:
An instructor within LSA who believes academic misconduct has occurred may choose either
Instructor Resolution: Resolve the matter directly with the student
Appropriate when: the incident is not egregious and merits no consequence greater than a zero on the assignment, though the student may be required to do additional, remedial work (e.g., rewrite a paper).
SAA Resolution: File a complaint to the Office of Student Academic Affairs, who will resolve the case. 
Appropriate when: the sanction may result in the student failing the course or more severe sanction, the student has a previous finding of responsibility, or the student is suspected of falsifying or misrepresenting academic documents

.
 
Examples of academic misconduct include, but are not limited to: cheating, plagiarism, inappropriate collaboration, falsification of data, records, or documents, and aiding and abetting dishonesty.
Deadlines: The complaint for any alleged instance of academic misconduct should be filed as soon as practical from the date of occurrence and should be submitted within 2 months of the date of the incident.
Privacy: Materials related to a formal complaint of academic misconduct or an instructor's report of a resolution will be maintained by the Office of Student Academic Affairs in compliance with the privacy expectations under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA).
While a mis

conduct case is pending, with either Instruction Resolution or SAA Resolution:
The student is presumed to not be responsible for the alleged misconduct and the student may continue to attend class and receive grades.
The instructor may NOT impose any penalty or require any remedial work until the case has been resolved.
The student may NOT change registration in the course (e.g. drop the course or change the grading option to Pass/Fail).
If the term ends and a final grade must be reported while a case is pending, the instructor should use the grade NR (No Report). NR is a temporary, neutral grade that may be used in special circumstances where a final grade is not yet able to be reported. Th

e student may not receive credit for the course in which the alleged misconduct occurred and may not graduate.
Note: Students found responsible for academic misconduct with either resolution are not eligible to drop or choose pass/fail grading for the course.

What an SAA Resolution is
A faculty or staff member within LSA who believes academic misconduct has occurred may file a formal complaint of academic misconduct with the LSA Office of Student Academic Affairs who will determine if misconduct has occurred.
Important: The instructor should not impose any penalty or require remedial work until the case has been resolved. Once a case has been filed with the Office of Student Academic Affairs, it may not be withdrawn without the approval of the Assistant Dean. Barring unforeseen circumstances, cases will be resolved within the academic term (and typically within three weeks) in which the incident occurs.
SAA Resolution Procedures
Reporting academi

c misconduct
Instructor reports a possible case of academic misconduct to SAA using the Report of Suspected Misconduct form
Prior to the Academic Misconduct Meeting
SAA sends an email to the student stating that an instructor has reported what they believe to be a possible case of academic misconduct. The email also includes a link to set up an Academic Misconduct Meeting. 
Once an appointment is scheduled, SAA sends a confirmation email which contains evidence about the allegations of misconduct. 
The Academic Misconduct Meeting will determine whether the student is responsible, or not, for the alleged misconduct. An accused student should prepare for the Academic Misconduct Meeting by revi

ewing the information provided, asking any clarifying questions, and show up ready to present any of their own relevant information, read any statement, and/or ask further questions. 
During the Academic Misconduct Meeting
The Coordinator of Academic Integrity or designee will describe the allegations made, detail the supporting evidence, and review the range of college-level sanctions (e.g. disciplinary probation, suspension, or expulsion).
This is an opportunity for the student to be heard and to present their side of the incident. The student should be ready to present any relevant material, read a statement, and/or ask questions.
Typically, in each meeting a representative of the LSA Stu

dent Honor Council participates, though they do not advocate for or against the student.
Students should notify the Office of Student Academic Affairs if they will have a support person in attendance at the meeting.
In certain circumstances, the Coordinator of Academic Integrity may give the student the opportunity to ask questions of the accusing party, either by exchanging written questions or by asking questions during a subsequent meeting. This additional step will be completed prior to the Coordinator or designee’s final decision.
The meeting between the accused student and the Coordinator of Academic Integrity or designee may be virtual or in-person.
Making a decision
The Coordinator o

f Academic Integrity or designee determines whether a violation of the LSA Community Expectations of Academic Integrity has occurred and if the student is responsible for academic misconduct.
The standard of review is preponderance. This means that the student is not considered responsible unless the evidence demonstrates that it is "more likely than not" that academic misconduct has occurred.
The student will be informed by letter, with an email copy to the instructor(s), of the decision and sanction(s), if any, to be imposed.
If a student is found not responsible for academic misconduct, the instructor(s) will grade the student accordingly.

If a student is found responsible for academic misconduct:
Course-level sanctions: appropriate grade penalties for the misconduct will be left up to the instructor based on syllabus grade policies or department policies, if applicable.
College-level sanctions: The student may be assigned college sanctions by the Office of Student Academic Affairs. Examples of these sanctions include: 
Disciplinary probation - students are placed on probation for one year. As part of this process, a notation is placed on the student's unofficial transcript. This notation serves as a warning and reprimand that the student has been found responsible for academic misconduct. After that one year period, the notat

ion is removed provided no further violations of academic misconduct have occurred.
Reflective Essay - the student must write an essay about their experience, share what they have learned from it, and discuss how they intend to incorporate LSA Community Expectations into their personal and academic life moving forward.
Suspension - the student is ineligible to enroll at the university for one semester and a permanent notation is added to their transcript. In order to re-enroll in future terms, the student must write a petition for reactivation at least two weeks prior to the start of the term they wish to enroll.
Expulsion - The student is permanently removed from the university.

A student who has been found responsible for academic misconduct may submit a written appeal to the LSA Academic Judiciary Committee (AJC), a committee composed of both undergraduate students and faculty members from the College of LSA.
Note: If students submit an appeal request, college- and course-level sanctions remain in place while it is pending. If an appeal is based on discrimination or other prohibited behavior, students must also file a report with the Equity, Civil Rights & Title IX Office (ECRT). The appeal process will pause until that matter is resolved.
Procedures
The student must submit an appeal within two weeks from the date of the resolution letter.
The appeal must state wh

at is being appealed: the finding of academic misconduct, the college sanction imposed, or both.
The appeal must also state and describe in detail at least one of the following grounds for appeal:
The procedure was violated in a way that seriously compromised the investigation and/or conclusions.
There is significant new evidence not reasonably available at the time of the meeting with the Coordinator of Academic Integrity or designee.
The college sanctions are excessive relative to the violation.
Appeals are not granted unless one or more of the above criteria are met and supported by evidence. 
Making a decision
A member of the AJC will decide whether the appeal has sufficient grounds to m

ove forward. If it does not, the appeal process ends and the Office of Student Academic Affairs' decision stands. There is no further appeal opportunity.
If it is determined that grounds for an appeal have been met, a panel of AJC members will review your case alongside evidence from the instructor and documentation of how the Office of Student Academic Affairs reached its decision.
After reviewing the appeal, the AJC may:
Reverse the finding of responsibility (overturn the original decision), or
Uphold the finding of responsibility. If it's upheld, the Committee may recommend that the Office of Student Affairs keep the sanction as is, reduce it, or increase it.
Students will be notified of
the outcome by email.

If a student registered in another school is accused of misconduct in an LSA course:
SAA's authority includes deciding whether or not the alleged action is a violation of Academic Integrity and whether course-level sanctions may be applied if the student is found responsible for misconduct.
Course-level sanctions are left up to the instructor.
SAA will recommend a sanction or sanctions to the School or College in which the student is registered, but that School or College has the responsibility for imposing any recommendation or additional sanction it determines appropriate.

coursework.en: The instructor determines permitted GenAI uses by course, assessment and activity, aligned with college misconduct policy. Read the syllabus and task instructions. Published permitted/restricted/banned examples are templates, not universal campus rules.
coursework.zh: 教师按课程、考核及活动明确AI许可，并与学院诚信政策一致。核对大纲和任务说明；官网允许、限制与禁用示例是模板，不是全校统一规则。
coursework.meaningEn: Course-specific authority; no general account-based academic permission.
coursework.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

exams.en: Follow the specific exam and college instructions. Current recaptured guidance establishes assessment-level instructor authority, but no exact exam authorization was revalidated. The Rackham explicit-permission claim remains held after source-access failure.
exams.zh: 遵守具体考试及学院说明。已重验材料确立按考核制定政策的权限，但未重验具体考试许可；Rackham明确许可条款因来源获取失败仍待核。
exams.meaningEn: Direct assessment guidance only; no revalidated exam-specific rule. Unclear scores0; held Rackham evidence not presented as current proof.
exams.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

disclosure.en: University principles call for appropriate disclosure and citation. Follow the actual course’s rules; sample disclosure appendices or bans are not automatically mandatory throughout U-M.
disclosure.zh: 校级原则要求适当披露及引用；具体做法核对实际课程。示例中的附录或禁用条款不自动成为全校强制格式。
disclosure.meaningEn: General principle versus instructor-selected assignment requirements; no universal disclosure template established.
disclosure.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

privacy_data.en: Use approved services and check each permitted data type; external services without a U-M contract should receive only Low institutional data. No model training does not mean no prompt/history/log processing or vendor sharing. Uniform retention duration and authenticated sensitive-data matrices remain unresolved.
privacy_data.zh: 使用获批服务并逐项核对数据类别；无校方合同的外部服务仅宜处理Low级校内数据。不用于训练不代表不处理提示、历史和日志或不向服务商共享；统一留存期限及登录后数据矩阵仍未确立。
privacy_data.meaningEn: ITS/Google institutional accounts; PHI safeguard statement is not blanket permission; original remaining claim8 hold preserved.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

approved_tools.en: ITS offers U-M GPT, Maizey and GPT Toolkit for active U-M users, subject to U.S.-only terms. Google eligibility excludes sponsored affiliates, alumni and retirees. Tool access, data approval and assessment permission are separate.
approved_tools.zh: ITS向活跃用户提供U-M GPT、Maizey与GPT Toolkit，条款限美国境内使用。Google服务不含受赞助附属人员、校友及退休者。工具访问、数据审批和考核许可分别判断。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Service eligibility and U.S.-only terms; seats/current API quotas not authenticated.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

research_publication.en: Apply honesty, appropriate citation and human responsibility in research. OVPR discourages GenAI peer reviewing and strongly discourages commercial upload of another researcher’s grant application. Its secure-tool language/clarity exception and sponsor conditions remain. HRPP/Rackham-specific claims are held.
research_publication.zh: 研究遵守诚实、适当引用及人的责任。OVPR不鼓励AI同行评审，并强烈不鼓励把其他研究者申请书上传商业AI；保留安全工具改善语言及资助方条件等例外。HRPP及Rackham专门结论仍待核。
research_publication.meaningEn: OVPR internal peer review PDF2025-08-11 and general scholarship guidance; not universal thesis/publication rule.
research_publication.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

academic_integrity.en: LSA distinguishes Instructor and SAA Resolution, presumes no responsibility while pending, and permits a response/support person. Course and college outcomes differ. LSA appeal is two weeks from the resolution-letter date. Rackham’s separate clock is not substituted; detector output is inquiry, not proof.
academic_integrity.zh: LSA区分教师与SAA处理，未决时推定不负责任，学生可回应及带支持者。课程和学院后果不同；LSA从决定信日期起两周申诉。不套用Rackham另一时钟；检测结果只可促成调查，不能证明作弊。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: LSA-only procedure/sanction/appeal; original held detector object remains held; new captured ITS explanation separate.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

teaching_guidance.en: U-M does not recommend unreliable AI detectors; this is not a ban. Instructors should make course rules clear. School of Nursing guidance says AI should not be the sole grading basis and identifiable student work needs approved service/use; do not extend this unit rule campus-wide.
teaching_guidance.zh: 学校不建议使用误差高的AI检测器，并非全面禁止。教师应清晰说明课程规则。护理学院指南称不应仅据AI评分，上传可识别学生作业须服务及用途获批；不将其扩大为全校规则。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: General teaching guidance and separately labelled School of Nursing faculty restrictions.
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

security_procurement.en: Human-review AI-generated code; use professionally trained peer review for all new/significantly changed applications, especially High/Restricted data. Procurement Services should be the sole buyer for institutional AI handling Moderate/High/Restricted data. Per-service approval remains separate.
security_procurement.zh: AI生成代码须人工检查；所有新增或重大修改应用应由专业人员同行审查，尤其High/Restricted数据应用。处理Moderate/High/Restricted校内数据的AI服务应仅由采购部门购买；具体服务数据许可另核对。
security_procurement.meaningEn: Should procurement modality retained; authenticated data matrix and IRB-specific approvals not inferred.
security_procurement.meaningZh: 适用范围以本主题的院系、课程、账户和版本原文为准，不跨范围推定许可。

do.en: Check the actual course and assessment rules.
do.zh: 核对实际课程及考核规则。

do.en: Follow task disclosure instructions and cite appropriately.
do.zh: 按任务披露要求适当引用。

do.en: For LSA, count the appeal period from the resolution-letter date.
do.zh: LSA申诉从决定信日期起算。

dont.en: Do not turn service access into assessment permission.
dont.zh: 不要把服务访问当作考核许可。

dont.en: Do not equate no training with no history or logs.
dont.zh: 不要把不用于训练理解为无历史或日志。

dont.en: Avoid uploading another researcher’s proposal to commercial AI.
dont.zh: 避免把其他研究者申请书上传商业AI。

scope.en: Course, college, service and research unit determine the applicable rule. LSA procedures do not replace Rackham or other schools.
scope.zh: 课程、学院、服务及研究单位决定适用规则；LSA程序不代替Rackham或其他学院规则。

umich-claim-1.text: U-M does not recommend the use of AI-detection technology given their high error rate. False positives and negatives are possible, and even likely.

evidence.quote: Language models generalize and summarize existing knowledge based on probability predictions of word sequences rather than copying it verbatim, and so it may be impossible to identify their use with certainty. While detection tools like Turnitin or GPTZero may report probability of AI authorship, they are easily circumvented and cannot provide definitive proof of cheating. False positives and negatives are possible, and even likely. U-M does not recommend the use of AI-detection technology at this time given their high error rate.
